original_card.question: Can a completed call earn more independent productive target credit without an offsetting paid bill?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Use #5599 as a completed positive control, then choose one uncovered cut/module beyond an applicable frozen exclusion. Derive independence, saturation and chronological availability rather than counting rational rank alone. Price target credits and all new jobs together, then check compiler and actual caller compatibility. Stop on a nonphysical credit or an unfavorable complete relaxation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Exact pointwise-in-exponent extreme of a declared paid/target invoice class on the documented signed concave screen, with uniqueness, sharpness and comparator composition.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a changed target-credit contract with a complete physical invoice and caller. This package instead settles the arithmetic screening question for every declaration that shares the four summary numbers (paid entry count, paid rank mass, target entry count, target rank mass). No physical credit, owner, restoration or supplier is claimed; the card's requirement to judge the complete signed target/paid bill is the link that is advanced.
bottleneck_link: The selected interface compares declared invoices by the signed target/paid moment. The package supplies the exact best-case invoice of a declared class and an O(1) class certificate, so a proposal whose declared moment would need more than its class ceiling is rejected before another construction round without replaying the word.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified class-extremal theorem and its comparator composition; do not extend to multiplicity caps, distinct-rank budgets or physical inventories.
evidence: PROOF.md; exhaustive exchange and class census over four boxes; comparator composition on schema-valid invoices; generated source-hash-bound RESULT.json.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a per-rank multiplicity cap on hostable targets lower the class ceiling, and by how much?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Independent helper refinements are bounded by how many targets of one rank a controller can host; a cap can only reduce the credit.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the exact maximum of sum s_j^x under per-rank caps for one audited invoice.
open_questions.blocked_by: No declared per-rank target cap inventory is bound for a concrete word.

open_questions.question: Which summary quadruples (Kp, Mp, Kt, Mt) are physically achievable for a fixed controller?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An unachievable canonical invoice is still a valid bound but a weaker one; an achievable set turns the ceiling into a sharper screen.
open_questions.first_step: Count the four numbers for one audited invoice and compare its net against its own class ceiling.
open_questions.blocked_by: No source inventory is bound in this package.

open_questions.question: Can a bound that also fixes the number of distinct ranks separate proposals the four summary numbers cannot?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The canonical invoices use at most two distinct ranks per side, so the summary quadruple loses distinct-rank information.
open_questions.first_step: Solve the same extremal problem with a distinct-rank budget and a tie-breaking rule.
open_questions.blocked_by: The extremal vector is no longer unique, so the equality characterisation needs a tie-breaking rule.
